rules.name: Sample mean definition
rules.operation: Compute the arithmetic mean of a finite sample.
examples: The sample mean aggregates observations into an average estimator of location
counterexamples: Dividing by n-1 instead of n defines a different statistic and is invalid here

rules.name: Sample variance with Bessel correction
rules.operation: Compute the corrected sample variance in the standard iid setting.
examples: Bessel correction is the standard unbiased finite-sample adjustment for variance in the iid setting
counterexamples: Omitting the centering term gives an invalid variance statistic

rules.name: Likelihood function construction rule
rules.input_form: model p_theta(x) and observed data x
rules.output_form: likelihood as a function of theta
preconditions: A statistical model indexed by theta is specified and data are fixed
rules.operation: View the model density or mass as a function of the parameter with data fixed.
examples: Bernoulli observations produce a likelihood in the parameter p after fixing the data
counterexamples: Treating the likelihood as a probability distribution over theta without normalization is invalid

rules.name: Maximum likelihood invariance seed
preconditions: theta_hat is an mle and g is a suitable function of the parameter
rules.operation: Transfer an mle through a parameter transformation by invariance.
examples: Estimating a variance parameter may induce an mle for the corresponding standard deviation through invariance
counterexamples: Applying invariance to non-function-valued set estimators is invalid

rules.name: Unbiased estimator criterion
preconditions: The estimator expectation exists across the model family
rules.operation: Check unbiasedness by comparing estimator expectation to the target parameter function.
examples: Unbiasedness compares the estimator's expected value to the target parameter across the model family
counterexamples: Checking equality at only one parameter value is insufficient

rules.name: p-value interpretation rule
rules.input_form: test statistic under a null model
rules.output_form: null-model tail probability at least as extreme as observed
preconditions: A null hypothesis, extremeness rule, and test statistic are specified
rules.operation: Interpret the p-value as a null tail probability rather than a posterior belief in the null.
examples: Small p-values indicate tension between the observed data and the null model under the chosen test statistic
counterexamples: Interpreting the p-value as the probability that the null hypothesis is true is invalid

rules.name: Neyman-Fisher factorization criterion seed
preconditions: The model admits the standard factorization analysis
rules.operation: Test sufficiency by factoring the data dependence of the likelihood through a candidate statistic.
examples: Exponential-family models often expose sufficient statistics through multiplicative likelihood factorization
counterexamples: Observing that a statistic is correlated with the parameter is insufficient for sufficiency

rules.name: Fisher information seed
rules.output_form: expected score variance or log-likelihood curvature quantity
preconditions: The model satisfies the standard differentiability hypotheses
rules.operation: Measure local parameter identifiability through expected score variability or likelihood curvature.
examples: Sharper likelihood concentration corresponds to larger information about the parameter
counterexamples: Treating information as independent of the model parameter in general is invalid

rules.name: Confidence interval coverage interpretation
preconditions: The interval procedure is defined relative to repeated sampling under the model
rules.operation: Interpret confidence levels through repeated-sampling coverage rather than posterior belief.
examples: Confidence levels describe procedure performance across repetitions, not posterior beliefs after one sample
counterexamples: Interpreting one realized 95 percent confidence interval as containing the true parameter with posterior probability 0.95 is invalid in the frequentist reading

rules.name: Bayes posterior update rule
rules.output_form: posterior proportional to likelihood times prior
preconditions: A prior and likelihood are defined on a common parameter space
rules.operation: Update prior beliefs by multiplying with the data likelihood and normalizing.
examples: Bayesian updating combines prior structure with data evidence through multiplication and normalization
counterexamples: Adding prior and likelihood instead of multiplying is invalid

rules.name: Linear regression normal equations seed
rules.input_form: least-squares model X beta approximately y
preconditions: The ordinary least-squares linear model is active
rules.operation: Convert classical linear regression fitting into a normal-equations system.
examples: Regression estimation reduces to a least-squares system in the classical linear model
counterexamples: Treating arbitrary nonlinear models as satisfying the same normal equations is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Composition rule expansion
rules.input_form: objects A and B with a valid composition law
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Compose structured objects when composition preconditions are satisfied.
examples: Function and operator compositions require compatible codomain-domain interfaces
counterexamples: Composing incompatible objects is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Inverse admissibility expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Introduce inverses only when invertibility conditions are explicitly satisfied.
examples: Matrix inversion requires nonsingularity
counterexamples: Assuming inverses exist without conditions is invalid

rules.name: Constraint propagation expansion

preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata

rules.name: Boundary condition integration expansion
rules.input_form: model equation with boundary or endpoint constraints
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Include boundary and endpoint constraints in the active model state before solving.
examples: Differential models require boundary or initial data to identify admissible solution families
counterexamples: Solving while ignoring required boundary conditions is invalid

rules.name: Conservation tracking expansion
rules.input_form: model evolution with candidate conserved quantity Q
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Track whether declared conserved quantities remain invariant under model evolution.

rules.name: Approximation error budget expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Attach explicit error bounds or estimates to approximation-driven outputs.
examples: Numerical approximations should report residual or tolerance-constrained error

rules.name: Parameter sensitivity expansion
rules.input_form: model output O(theta) with parameter vector theta
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Quantify how parameter perturbations affect outputs and derived conclusions.
examples: Small parameter shifts can cause large output changes near bifurcation or instability regions
counterexamples: Assuming robustness with no sensitivity analysis is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Symmetry detection expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Detect and record symmetry transformations that preserve model structure.
examples: Translation or rotation symmetries can simplify derivations and reduce state dimensionality
counterexamples: Attributing symmetry to a model that breaks it under constraints is invalid

rules.name: Dimensionless reduction expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rescale equations by characteristic magnitudes to expose dimensionless groups.

counterexamples: Mixing inconsistent scales yields invalid normalization

rules.name: Solver branch admissibility expansion
rules.input_form: problem state and candidate branch family
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Choose solver branches by matching structural form, assumptions, and goal type.
examples: Optimization, proof, and simulation branches require different admissibility logic
counterexamples: Selecting branches on keywords alone is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Degenerate case handling expansion
rules.input_form: rule with potential degenerate parameter regimes
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Split and handle degenerate regimes explicitly instead of forcing generic formulas.
examples: Singular, zero, or limiting parameter cases often require separate derivation paths
counterexamples: Applying generic rules to singular cases without modification is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Proof obligation expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Convert claims into explicit proof obligations before acceptance.
